newsitem.title: CHINA: HK blue chips end modestly higher, property soft.
newsitem.headline: HK blue chips end modestly higher, property soft.

text.p: Hong Kong blue chips ended with modest gains on Monday as shares in HSBC Holdings Plc powered ahead to a record high, but property market uncertainty returned to plague share prices which ended off the day's highs.

The blue chip Hang Seng Index closed 35.61 points, or 0.24 percent, higher at 14,858.58 after falling to a low of 14,723.46 points and rising to a high of 15,003.02. Turnover was HK$20.02 billion compared with HK$22.51 billion on Friday.
"There is still uncertainty about the property market and that is why the market is wandering about in a range," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
"At 14,700 there was buying from overseas and local investors and investors were taking profit at 15,000 points."

Analysts said while property stocks had attempted a rebound on Monday, they were unable to sustain their gains and more weakness lay ahead until the government made its property policy clear. Hong Kong chief executive Tung Chee-hwa said last week that he would implement measures to cool down the property market but did not say how he would do this.
"About two thirds of the market is related to property so if the property outlook looks unclear there is no reason to chase it," said Archie Hart, associate director at BZW Securities.
"It seems like we are not really going to get Tung's view on property until October so the uncertainty is going to linger for a while," said Hart.
Tung is due to deliver a policy statement in October.
Shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd ended down HK$0.50 at HK$85.75 and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd ended unchanged at HK$71.75.
New World Development Co Ltd gained HK$0.10 to HK$46.40.
HSBC roared ahead to hit an all-time high of HK$247.00, before closing up HK$4.00 at HK$245.00.
"It is being pulled up by a strong U.K. market," said Hart.
Brokers said talk of a covered warrant issue had also pushed the share price.
The red chip Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index ended up 3.06 points, or 0.09 percent, at 3,420.49 after earlier rising to a high of 3,490.15.

Hart said red chips had suffered from the weak tone in Chinese markets, which fell on Monday after euphoria surrounding Hong Kong's July 1 return to Chinese rule disappeared, taking major support away from mainland share prices.
The July futures contract on the Hang Seng Index rose 30 points to close at 14,860.
